insights.statement: Promotional intensity escalated sharply in FY2025: promotions rose from 29% to 38% of sales and average depth from 18% to 24% of regular price, with promo share up in all four categories
insights.decision_relevance: Sets the baseline: 2026 plan starts from an already very high promotional level

insights.statement: Promotions did not drive growth: promoted volume grew 14% but full-price volume fell 6%, leaving total volume up only 2.1% — volume shifted to promotion rather than being created
insights.decision_relevance: Contradicts the core premise of the marketing proposal (H1 rejected)

insights.statement: Most promoted volume is subsidised demand: 71% is bought by customers who also buy the same item at full price, and sales of promoted items fall 22% in the two weeks after a promotion ends (forward buying)
insights.decision_relevance: Explains why more promotion budget buys little incremental volume

insights.statement: The cost is visible in margin: gross margin fell 2.3 pp from 27.4% to 25.1% while promotional depth rose 6 pp
insights.decision_relevance: Quantifies the value at stake for the CFO
insights.caveat: Correlation; sources lack a margin bridge, so non-promotional drivers (H6) are not excluded

insights.statement: Returns split by category: per hundred euros of promoted sales, Household (−3.4 EUR) and Snacks (−2.1 EUR) lose incremental margin, while Fresh (+1.6 EUR) and Beverages (+0.8 EUR) gain it
insights.decision_relevance: Defines where to cut and where to keep promotion in 2026

insights.statement: The marketing proposal would scale the worst economics: a 20% budget increase and deep discounts in Household, the category with the most negative incremental margin (−3.4 EUR per hundred euros of promoted sales)
insights.decision_relevance: Board should not approve the proposal as submitted
